title: Windows smoke teardown can encounter a runtime lock after protocol checks pass
body: The first v0.14.0 publish attempt on 2026-09-07 passed every Windows ARM64 product assertion, including uninstall and subsequent project MCP/hook operation, then failed in final temporary-directory removal with EBUSY on a copied project runtime's node.exe. The release gate correctly blocked publication. Re-running only the failed job on the same tagged source passed, including cleanup; the other five platforms had passed on the first attempt. A lingering process or transient Windows file lock is plausible, but the precise cause was not established. Do not classify this observed teardown failure as an installer-uninstall failure, or treat the earlier 'smoke passed' log line as a successful job exit. Proposed follow-up: inspect MCP child-process shutdown and use bounded, observable teardown handling while keeping product uninstall assertions strict. A rerun passing is evidence of intermittency, not proof that the underlying teardown race is fixed.

sources.note: Windows ARM64 passed product assertions but final fs.rm failed with EBUSY on the temporary project runtime.
The same tagged source passed on the failed-job retry and publication completed.
